rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words, grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.  (view grep banned_words body_hits=1; my own grep -n 'crucial' over lines 1-65 returns exactly line 5)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop the adverb; the sentence is stronger bare.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony, hard ban in any curriculum/training surface.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 11: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.  (view grep ritual_ceremony body_hits=1; confirmed at line 11)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Word is *exercise*; and the line also claims a per-session cadence this atomic M1 beat does not have.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no fixed retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 49: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.  (view greps session_biography=1 and dated_line=1; both land on line 49, which is body, not maintainer)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the sentence outright; git carries the history.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5 crucially / 11 ritual / 37 no penalty, and it is completely fine either way. Three lines pull the AE101 quintet toward consultancy-deck and L&D-coach register.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Register damage is downstream of rules 1, 2 and 9; fixing those clears it. No separate edit owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always you, never the student; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 24: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.  (view grep the_student body_hits=1; confirmed at line 24)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Third-person teacher framing in body. It is also factually wrong for this slot, and cutting it is cheaper than recasting it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 37: There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.  (no penalty is a verbatim flag phrase in the rule's list)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the whole sentence; line 39 already gives the reader the move.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 55: ## Anything can be reverse-engineered, and 57: Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM. The section holds exactly two bullets (lines 57, 58); no boundary paragraph follows the slogan.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Restore one Boris-direct carve-out bullet naming the boundary the backing block already states (extraction quality tracks the quality of the source data sampled).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing; run the truth test before reaching for rule 12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line: 57, Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM. The superlative survives the truth test because the same clause scopes it to what can be inspected and then enumerates inspectable artifacts. It overreaches on a subset rather than having no true reading, so rule 12 is the right instrument, not this one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The What happened block is optional; default is to omit it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 62-64. Three moves present: count plus noun (Two things came out of one ticket), one qualifier (the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along), and a destination (The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.). 42 words, past tense, lands forward.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest header: 55, Anything can be reverse-engineered. It is a slogan, not a spatial metaphor contradicting the mechanism, and no other X construction appears. Its problem is the missing boundary, filed under rule 12, not a false header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line: 39, Push back on the five. Push back is directed at the proposals, not at the agent, and is house vocabulary for review moved upstream. Every other student-to-agent verb in the body is ask, tell, or drop.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM vs agent vs Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 57 keeps LLM on the capability/thinking sentence; 58 uses the agent for the three action steps; 33 and 45 use Ask Claude for the addressee. The backing block at line 125 records this exact split as a deliberate reshape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5: the step that changes how the run behaves. Noun-run naming the agent's sitting. Verified against curriculum/vocabulary.md line 25: Noun-run for the agent sitting is banned in student-facing body. The only other run in the body is verb-run at line 57 (the system your team runs on), which is legal.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Session, or recast around the task; the line is being rewritten for rule 1 anyway.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Connector at line 43 is covered by the dated accept-note at line 72 (Antti 2026-08-18: engineer audience knows MCP/connectors, do not re-file). Every other term (tracker, ticket, repro steps, CI pipeline) is ordinary engineer vocabulary the rule's assumed-known carve-out exempts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body, with a boundary exception.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest lines: 18 (If there is no ticket for this bug, say so in the chat) and 30 (No ticket of your own to read?). Both clear the base test, plausible failure plus non-obvious rescue in one tight line, so they stay in body rather than routing below the fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every instruction line names an actor and a mechanism; look-lines name the object and the tell.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line: 53, Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it. Object is the comments already on the ticket, tell is the wording feels off, speech verb carries its addressee (tell Claude). This is the passage the rule's own 2026-08-14 note says was previously read as blanket-exempt; re-run here, it holds.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body read it / look at it / notice X after chat-print is dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line: 24, At this point the student should notice the test is still red, sits directly after the prompt at line 22. It is filed under check_writing rule 7 as third-person teacher framing, which is the sharper instrument; the same cut discharges this rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself; subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line: 64, The next exercise sweeps this whole session. Subject is an exercise, which normally fails the subject test, but check_writing rule 16 move 3 explicitly blesses landing a recap on what reads the artifact next (the artifact STRIDE reads next). Carve-out applies; no finding.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 43: [MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md). Link text is the target's H1 title, not a filename or code-span path. The ../ prefix is path form, governed by module-shape, and this rule's own 2026-08-13 note warns judges off filing it here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: View grep em_dash body_hits=0 for the punctuation half of the table; on vocabulary, the only terms-of-art in body (reverse-engineer, close-out, convention) are plain-English at M1 arc position and nothing from later modules is echoed in a lead-in or header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest lines: 62, Two things came out of one ticket, and 33/39, propose five bug rules / Push back on the five. Neither count sits above a bullet list the reader can see. Two names the artifacts inline in the same sentence, and five is a real quantity the prompt asks the agent to produce, then a handle the reader carries to line 39 where the items are not visible. That is the memory-handle carve-out.

findings.quote: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.
findings.harm: Banned consultancy register in student-facing prose; it flinches the engineer audience and reads as a deck, not a peer. Present: crucially is on the zero-tolerance list and survives at line 5, meaning the Write/Edit auto-fix never ran over this text.

findings.quote: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.
findings.harm: Ritual ships the compound loop as Scrum ceremony, which is the exact register the training exists to replace. Present: hard-banned word in body, and the claim is also false for this atomic third-of-four M1 beat.
findings.fix: Cut the line; if a repeat cadence is wanted, say it as an exercise you can re-run, and check it against the maintainer block's arc note first.

findings.quote: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.
findings.harm: Session biography in student-facing body. A reader who never saw the old version loses nothing and gains a distraction, and the changelog rots the moment the section moves again. Present: both the transition verb (previously, was fixed) and the bare date are in body region, above the line-66 maintainer cut.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence. Rules are rules, history is git.

findings.quote: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.
findings.harm: Third-person teacher framing leaks the trainer's POV into prose the student reads about themselves, and it survives copy-paste as narration rather than instruction. Present: the student in body, plus a delivery-mechanics sentence that belongs below the fence. Compounding: the maintainer block says this exercise runs after fix-tests-first with the PR shipped, so the test is green here, and the line asks the student to notice something that is not on screen.
findings.fix: Cut the line. If a state check is genuinely owed, recast as second person and against a true state.

findings.quote: There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.
findings.harm: Reassurance signals the author thought the ask needed defending, and a senior reader registers the defensiveness rather than the permission. Present: no penalty is a verbatim flag phrase, doubled by a second absolving clause in the same sentence.
findings.fix: Cut the sentence whole. Line 39 already gives the reader the move and the reason.

findings.harm: A slogan with no boundary paragraph downstream gets over-read, and this one generalises a single-practitioner L1 stance to every artifact. Present: the section runs to two bullets (57, 58) and stops. The file's own backing stance at line 134 asserts the boundary is carried in the third bullet, so the design relied on a carve-out that is not in the body.
findings.fix: Add one Boris-direct bullet after 58 naming the boundary the stance already states: extraction quality tracks the quality of the source you sampled. Then reconcile the stance clause so the next judge does not re-derive it.

findings.quote: the step that changes how the run behaves
findings.harm: Noun-run for the agent's sitting blurs the session/task/run split the training installs, and engineers do not say it. Present: line 5 uses it for the agent's work, not for a test or CI execution.
findings.fix: Session, or recast around the task. The line is being rewritten for §1 anyway.

todos.note: Maintainer/backing stance says the slogan carries its boundary in the third bullet; the section has two. Whoever fixes the §12 finding must strike or rewrite this clause in the same pass, or the next judge re-derives a stale keep. Out of body region, hence a todo, not a finding.
